convoLines.text: "What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time. Anyway, I should move."
"Spite, mostly. Pure, clean spite at the sky. Then someone shared food with me and the spite turned into something else. I still don't have a word for the something else."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"We went over this," Carmine says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
Carmine looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"That again?" Carmine sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"It's stupid. I'm alive, everyone's alive, and I can't stop shaking. Simple as that."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
They pat the ground beside them. "Here. It's dry."
"My hands stopped shaking. That's — that's something. Thank you for sitting here. I won't forget that."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Mburu. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Still on that hard time. ...sorry, I'm spiraling."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Salvatore is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"I don't answer that one myself. Not yet. Maybe when I've decided whether surviving counts as an excuse or just a reason. I mean it."
"Still on the worst thing you've done."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"Salvatore always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sleep's gone strange. I pace while thinking at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The fire feels smaller without Salvatore. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on teaching them something."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Salvatore died... I keep expecting to see Salvatore at the fire. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Carmine grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Carmine is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sleep's gone strange. I check the treeline every hour at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I don't want to be alone with my head right now. That's all. That's the whole thing."
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Careful — that log's hotter than it looks." They shift it with a boot, making space.
"I keep going over it. Having someone here... it slows the spiral."
"that hard time — that's still where we are."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Salvatore was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Carmine nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Nobody says Salvatore's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I'm picking up Salvatore's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on what you believe in. Gotta keep moving."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Tyler — The Wrong Map, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Mburu nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I show up. That's my part."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Okay, but what about I'm not okay. I'm saying it out loud so it's real: I'm not okay."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"Nice. Sit. The fire's warm."
"It helps. Just — saying it out loud to someone who's actually listening. It helps."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Mburu presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Like I said — we're still on that hard time."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Wrong Map. They just... took Tyler. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Carmine nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Burdock today. You were right, it was right where you said."
They light up a little when they see you.
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Huh. Let me think about that." I don't want to be in charge. I want us to survive. Those look the same from the outside.
"I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Will you help me?"
"It's not about power. It's about — someone has to decide, and I'd rather it be someone who'll lose sleep over it."
"I caught myself counting heads at the fire last night, making sure everyone was back. Old habit. New reason."
"Still on wanting to be in charge."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that warning — I keep turning it over."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Thank you. I needed to hear you say it."
"I keep thinking about that The Loud Beast. It knows this ground now. Keep your eyes up past the treeline."
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Mburu doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Mburu is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway — I should get going."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you believe we get through this — the alternative doesn't work. Still holding the line?"
You can feel the history in how they greet you.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
They let that thread drop — for now.
"Alright, I'm listening. What's next?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Mburu nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"The cistern's nearly dry — 5 liters left. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"5 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."

"I should get back to it."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Good. What I've heard of them, I believe. Go and ask." You carry the proposal to Emberhold.
It's quiet at the trap line. Carmine doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
"Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's fishing. A plan's just a direction you argue with."
"Still on your plan here, anyway."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"

"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You look tired. Sit. Tell me something good."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Mburu doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 7 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."

"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Carmine nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"The creek water run — I haven't stopped thinking about it."
They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "My brain's buffering on that one. Ask me when it's loaded."
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.

"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."

"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"I don't keep score on that. Score-keeping is how you stop sleeping. I do what the day needs and I don't rehearse it after."
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Ask me again in a few days. Maybe I'll have a better answer by then."

"I saved you a spot. Sit."

"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Still on who you don't trust."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

d42: That night, they bring Salvatore home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d44: You say a few words for Salvatore. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d44: You bury Salvatore. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d46: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+2 integration)

deathBeatLines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Salvatore Burns is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Salvatore Burns is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Salvatore — and Salvatore is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.

echoSample: d44: "Salvatore is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d44: "Salvatore always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d44: "The fire feels smaller without Salvatore. The rest of us will have to be bigger."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Salvatore Burns is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Salvatore Burns is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Salvatore kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Salvatore's gone." Carmine looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Salvatore." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Sal blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Generous Heart (Level 1). Donating gives 2x trust.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Salvatore Burns, 41 days. The mantle passes to Sal Steele.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Sal Steele, 46 — an interpreter. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Scream Cheese.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Salvatore — and Salvatore is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Tyler, Carmine, Mburu and 3 more speak for Sal — "Salvatore trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Sal before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d110: 🤒 Omar is on the mend — the fever broke.
d110: 🤒 Tyler is achy and wrung out, barely eating. Rest and clean water — or it gets worse.
d111: — DAY 111 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d111: Carmine Holmes reads the sky: clear tomorrow, freezing.
d111: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. Your sleeping body burned less — 57 kcal conserved. By the fire. Good enough.)
